hook: The $89 cabinet kit doesn't come in burnt-orange

scenes.visual_prompt: Cabinet kit box on a counter, label showing fixed colors Dark, Linen, Espresso, White
scenes.voiceover: The $89 kit everyone's using ships in five colors — none of them burnt-orange.

scenes.visual_prompt: Phone screen scrolling Pinterest burnt-orange terracotta kitchen cabinets
scenes.voiceover: So where's the color everyone's posting actually coming from?

scenes.visual_prompt: Hand carrying a can of bonding coat into a paint store counter
scenes.voiceover: DIYers are taking the bonding coat itself in and having it tinted to a specific chip.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of a paint counter tinting machine dispensing orange pigment into a can
scenes.voiceover: That's also why results vary more than a pre-mixed paint — tint ratio and coat count both shift the final tone.

scenes.visual_prompt: Two side-by-side cabinet doors, one lighter terracotta, one deeper burnt-orange, same base kit
scenes.voiceover: Same $89 kit, two different outcomes, depending on how it's tinted and applied.

scenes.visual_prompt: Finished kitchen shot, burnt-orange cabinets catching window light
scenes.voiceover: Get the tint and the coats right, and this is what's possible for under $200.

caption: The burnt-orange cabinets flooding Pinterest this week aren't coming pre-mixed out of an $89 box — they're a custom tint job on top of it. Here's exactly what DIYers are asking the paint counter for, and why two people with the same kit get different results. Full writeup linked.
